title: Fly — kinowo worker diagnostics (quarantined: needs a 6PN peer)

panels.title: Read this before believing anything below

options.content:
# ⚠ QUARANTINED — this dashboard has no data source that works today

**Nothing on this page is broken. Nothing on it is connected either.** Every panel below reads one
of two datasources, and neither can reach anything from monitoring-1:

* **`fly-prometheus`** — Fly's managed Prometheus, the *only* source of `fly_instance_*`,
  `fly_edge_*` and `fly_app_*`, which are produced by Fly's own host agent and cannot be scraped
  from anywhere else. Both read-only Fly tokens were **revoked**, and the org token this estate
  still has **cannot mint a replacement** (`createLimitedAccessToken Not authorized`). An org-wide
  token must not live on this host: monitoring-1 also runs the k3s control plane, so anything that
  compromised a workload there would gain the ability to **deploy to Fly**, where the production
  web tier still runs. Scraping some gauges is not worth that.
* **`app-metrics-live`** — on Fly this was a VictoriaMetrics sidecar scraping the apps' `/metrics`
  endpoints directly over 6PN every 15s, because the same series read back from Fly's managed
  Prometheus run **15–25 minutes behind**. There is no such sidecar here. The datasource is still
  provisioned, pointing at the local Prometheus, purely so these panels render *"No data"* instead
  of *"Datasource app-metrics-live was not found"* — which would make the page unreadable rather
  than empty.

**Why this dashboard still exists.** The apps it watches are still running: `kinowo` (web) and
`kinowo-worker` are both still on Fly. Every panel is correct and will start working again the day
there is a credential — deleting them would be throwing away working instrumentation to tidy up a
credential problem. They live in this folder rather than beside the fleet dashboards so that a
screen full of *No data* is somewhere you go **on purpose**, not something you trip over while
looking at the machines.

**To bring it back.**

1. Mint a genuinely read-only token from an account that may: `fly tokens create readonly --org personal`.
2. Put it in `nix/secrets/monitoring-1.yaml` as `grafana/fly-token` (and `prometheus/fly-token` if
   you also want the federation scrape), then set `fleet.prometheus.scrapeFly = true`.
3. Re-read the note above `Serving app down` in `alert-rules.yaml`: its `noDataState` and
   `execErrState` were flipped to `OK` because the dead datasource turned them into a permanent
   page, and they must go **back to `Alerting`** in the same edit as the new token.

The `app-metrics-live` panels need something different and larger: a **Fly 6PN peer for
monitoring-1**, exactly as `roles/wireguard-fly.nix` builds one for mongo-1, so the local Prometheus
can scrape the apps directly. That is a known, named gap and it is not fixed.

**For the machines, use the “Kinowo Fleet — Hetzner hosts” dashboard**, which queries the local
Prometheus only and needs no credential at all.


---

**This page is the worst-affected of the three.** 32 of its 35 panel targets read `app-metrics-live`, i.e. the JVM's own NMT / heap / GC / cache instrumentation, which was *never* available through Fly's managed Prometheus even when the token worked — it came from the 6PN sidecar. A Fly token alone will restore only the three `fly_instance_*` panels here. The rest need the 6PN peer.

panels.title: Native memory by NMT category (committed)
panels.description: kinowo_worker_native_memory_bytes — the native buckets invisible to jvm_memory_*. The one that climbs toward each ~5-6h non-heap OOM restart is the culprit. Needs -XX:NativeMemoryTracking=summary.

panels.title: Resident set size (RSS) vs cgroup limit
panels.description: Two independent readings of the same number: process_resident_memory_bytes (the JVM's process exporter) and kinowo_worker_process_rss_bytes (VmRSS, read straight from /proc/self/status by the vitals sampler that also computes the off-book gap panel). They should sit on top of each other — they're drawn together so the gap panel's arithmetic is checkable rather than taken on faith, and so a divergence between the two sources shows up as a divergence instead of as a wrong gap. The dashed line is the ~960MB cgroup ceiling. A slow climb that resets at a restart = the native working set; a spike to the line = a Fly RSS-kill.

panels.title: CPU breakdown — centicores (process / JIT / GC)
panels.description: process CPU vs JIT-compilation vs GC, in centicores (100=1 core). Dashed = the 13cc shared-cpu-2x credit breakeven; sustained above it drains the credit bucket.

panels.title: Fly CPU-credit balance vs throttle floor
panels.description: fly_instance_cpu_balance. Dashed = the 8000 throttle-enter floor. Draining below it trips the scrape throttle.

panels.title: Uptime (hours) — drops mark restarts
panels.description: (now - process_start_time)/3600. Each drop to ~0 is a restart; the cadence (~5-6h) is the OOM cycle. Cross-check the reason with `flyctl machine status` (exit_code=3 = ExitOnOutOfMemoryError).

panels.title: JVM threads (current / peak)
panels.description: jvm_threads_current & _peak. A climbing thread count → 'unable to create native thread' OOM. The 2026-07-09 probe found these STABLE (~86-92), so the OOM is not a thread leak — watch for drift.

panels.title: Heap used
panels.description: jvm_memory_used_bytes{area=heap}. Healthy = sawtooth well under Xmx=320MB; a rising floor = a heap leak (NOT the current failure mode).

panels.title: Read-model projection — avg duration (ms)
panels.description: Per-call cost of the read-model projection. A 3-5x inflation at a FLAT call rate = the daytime GC-thrash flare (projection is a victim of GC pauses, not the cause).

panels.title: Off-book native memory — RSS minus NMT-committed
panels.description: kinowo_worker_native_offbook_gap_bytes: RSS minus everything HotSpot admits to committing. Neither of the panels at the top of this dashboard can show it — jvm_memory_* covers the heap, the NMT panel covers the committed native categories, and this is the remainder. It is the primary signal for the ~5-6h non-heap OOM restarts: the 2026-07-09 probe found every NMT category flat across a whole 5h life while RSS climbed ~26MB/hr, which is glibc malloc retention/fragmentation in the C heap and appears here and nowhere else. READ THE SLOPE, NOT THE LEVEL — the level is normally NEGATIVE (around −200 to −320MB in steady state) because committed is not resident: pages can be committed and never touched. That is why this axis is deliberately not floored at zero. A gap climbing steadily toward and past zero, resetting only at a restart, is the pre-OOM signature; where it would meet the cgroup ceiling on the RSS panel is roughly when the machine dies.

panels.title: Resolution cache — hit rate % by source
panels.description: Share of identity resolutions (film → TMDB id / IMDb id / rating-site url) served from cache instead of running a live probe chain. A chain costs up to ~30 upstream GETs for RT/Metacritic and ~36 for Filmweb, so this is the cache's actual saving. Low here means the cache is doing little — the resolved url is persisted on the film record anyway, which is the competing gate.

panels.title: Resolution chains RUN — by source and kind
panels.description: Probe chains actually executed, per second. `miss_resolved` mints a cached answer and should decay as the corpus resolves; `miss_unresolved` is a chain that found nothing and — because the cache is hits-only — was NOT cached, so the same film burns the same chain again next cycle. If miss_unresolved dominates, the fix is caching negative results, not deleting the cache.

panels.title: Durable-store share of cache hits % by source
panels.description: Of the hits, how many came from the Mongo `resolve_*` collections rather than the in-process Caffeine layer. This is what the durable half buys over a plain in-memory cache — it is the only part that survives a worker restart. Near 0% across sources means the 5 collections + TTL-index reconciliation are carrying nothing and could be dropped.

panels.title: Cinema-scrape HTTP outcomes — error share, scrape phase (per country)
panels.description: A failure-budget view scoped to phase="scrape": ONLY the cinema-site HTTP — every listing scrape, chunk scrape and per-film detail fetch — with the third-party metadata/rating/resolution APIs (phase="enrich") excluded; its companion enrich-phase panel below covers those. Each error band's thickness is that error's share of scrape attempts, stacked at the floor; the empty space above is the clean remainder. This isolates cinema-scrape health from the enrichment APIs' by-design 404 slug-probing and API 429s: here a rising http_403 (a cinema Cloudflare/datacentre-IP block) or http_5xx/timeout stands out instead of hiding under the enrichment 404 noise floor.

panels.title: Enrichment HTTP outcomes — error share, enrich phase (per country)
panels.description: The scrape panel's companion, scoped to phase="enrich": ONLY the third-party metadata/rating/resolution APIs (TMDB/IMDb/RT/Metacritic/Filmweb/Letterboxd/Wikidata/Cinemeta), with cinema-site scraping (phase="scrape") excluded. Each error band's thickness is that error's share of enrich attempts, stacked at the floor; the empty space above is the clean remainder. Reading this side on its own: a large steady http_404 band is EXPECTED — the RT/Metacritic resolvers probe up to 4 candidate slugs per title and the wrong ones 404 by design — while http_401 (a bad/missing API key) or a rising http_429 (an API rate-limiting us) is the signal to watch. Improbable codes (409/422/451/…) fold into the residual http_4xx; other categories: http_5xx=server, timeout=connect/read, connection_error=refused/DNS/reset/TLS, other=unclassified.

description: QUARANTINED after the 2026-08-29 migration off Fly. Every panel reads `fly-prometheus` (no working token) or `app-metrics-live` (no 6PN path from monitoring-1), so the whole page renders No data. Kept, not deleted: the apps it watches are still running on Fly and it starts working again the day there is a credential. The first panel explains how. For the Hetzner machines, use "Kinowo Fleet — Hetzner hosts".
